title: The future of music: composition and the American popular song
summary: He won't predict, but says the media are the same faults as for 30 years, and that lasting music needs composition, with American popular songs a vast resource.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Okay, let's see. I was going to ask you about a little deeper thing at the moment. This one has to do with future of American music as it relates to how composition might fit into it. Some people have felt that strong compositional structure of the music may be the order of the day toward looking toward the window of the future of music. I wonder how you feel about it?
Well, in the first place, I would hate to be in a position to have to make predictions on a longrange plan. I have no idea where we're going to wind up, anymore than anyone has does.

I feel that we're in a healthy position today, and the immediate future looks reasonably bright to me. There's a lot of faults, but they're the same faults we've had now for 25 or 30 years. And that is the medias -- and I include radio, television and the record industry above all.
And these are things that until they
start to improve, we can only just keep producing as good music as we possibly can.
Yeah. I guess I'm speaking and addressing the issue of the music per se, and it's a trend of the music with more emphasis on composition than just bulling blowing sessions.

Well, I think that this has always been the thing that helped to make something a lasting -- truly lasting situation. There have only been so many giants thus far in history as far as solo playing is concerned. And some of them will live as long probably as people listen to jazz. And I would hope so, because they were that different and outstanding and that good. But as it is to a more wide approval at different levels, then I think it takes a larger form of creativity, and that has to be composition, rather than individual performance.
Because the subsisting body of jazz literature, like Ellington's literature and others, are compositional, although in the context of particular solos and so forth, but yet, that material.
